title: 다녀와서 이야기하기: 사람이 많더라, 바다가 예쁘더군요
objective: By the end, you can use -더라 and -더군요 (with verbs, adjectives, nouns and the past -았/었더-) to report something you saw or felt yourself, and choose the right one for the listener.
summary: Learn to tell someone what you saw or experienced yourself in the past, using -더라 with friends and -더군요 in polite speech.

task.title: Report what you saw
task.line: Choose, correct or write the -더라 / -더군요 form that fits the listener and the situation.

forms.when: Casual speech (반말) with friends or younger people. Same form after any stem: 가더라, 먹더라, 좋더라.
forms.means: Telling someone now about something you saw or felt yourself in the past.
forms.example: 어제 가 본 식당, 생각보다 비싸더라.
forms.exampleMeaning: That restaurant I tried yesterday was pricier than I expected.

forms.when: Polite speech. -더군 without 요 sounds like talking to yourself, or like an older person speaking to a junior.
forms.means: Same as -더라, often with a feeling of 'I found out / I noticed'.
forms.example: 부산에 가 보니까 바다가 정말 아름답더군요.
forms.exampleMeaning: When I went to Busan, I found the sea really beautiful.

forms.when: The action was already finished when you saw it.
forms.means: When I got there, it had already happened.
forms.exampleMeaning: I went to the shop, but it had already closed.

forms.when: After a noun. After a vowel, 이 is usually dropped: 친구더라.
forms.means: I saw / found out that it was N.
forms.example: 알고 보니 그 사람이 민수 동생이더군요.
forms.exampleMeaning: It turned out that person was Minsu's younger sibling.

watchOut: 나는 어제 공부하더라 (X) → 나는 어제 공부했어 (O): Do not use -더라 for your own actions. You report what you watched, not what you did.
친구가 외롭더라 (X) → 친구가 외로워하더라 (O): For someone else's feelings, use -아/어하다 + 더라. Your own feelings are fine: 나는 그 영화가 무섭더라.
선생님, 그 식당 맛있더라 (X) → 선생님, 그 식당 맛있더군요 (O): -더라 is casual speech. To older people or at work, use -더군요.
exercises: Choose the right form for the listener: ① (to a close friend) 그 가게 빵이 정말 (싸더라 / 싸더군요). ② (to your manager) 제주도는 바람이 많이 (불더라 / 불더군요).
Fill in the blank with -았/었더라 (the snow had already fallen when you looked): 아침에 창밖을 보니까 밤새 눈이 많이 ____. (오다)
Write O if the sentence is correct and X if it is wrong: ① 나는 지난 주말에 집 청소를 하더라. ② 동생이 시험에 떨어져서 많이 속상해하더라. ③ 주말에 시장이 정말 복잡하더라.
Fill in the blank with the noun + (이)더군요 form: 이야기해 보니까 그분이 우리 동네 치과 ____. (의사)
Choose the right one (they had all gone home before you arrived): 저녁에 회사에 다시 갔는데 동료들이 벌써 다 (퇴근하더라 / 퇴근했더라).
Rewrite the sentence with -더라 to tell a friend what you saw: 민수가 운동장에서 축구를 하고 있었어요.
answers: ① X ② O ③ O
민수가 운동장에서 축구를 하더라. (민수가 운동장에서 축구를 하고 있더라.)
